messages.content: Reprice the Atlanta-Birmingham trip one more time. Verify the dates, the one-way charge, and that the Birmingham counter is actually open when I return the car. If the schedule still works, book all three pieces.

I have the trip as Tuesday, September 16 through Wednesday, September 17: ORD to ATL Tuesday morning, one night at Home2 Suites Birmingham Downtown, then BHM to ORD Wednesday evening with an Avis midsize returned at Birmingham airport. I’ll check live totals and the return logistics before purchasing.
Correct. Keep the Tuesday noon inspection and Wednesday 9:00 to 1:30 inspection in the timing check.

The flights are still available, but the open-jaw fare has risen from $596 to $624 total. Tuesday departs ORD at 7:10 a.m. and arrives ATL at 10:15 a.m. Wednesday departs BHM at 5:35 p.m. and arrives ORD at 7:40 p.m. The fare is nonrefundable; if canceled before departure, the value can be retained as an airline credit subject to the ticket rules.
That increase is acceptable. What happened with Home2 and Avis?

Home2 still has the selected king studio for one night at $196.44 including taxes, plus $15 overnight parking. It can be canceled without charge until 6:00 p.m. local time on September 15; after that, the penalty is one night. Avis remains $274.62 for the ATL-to-BHM midsize rental, and the quoted total explicitly includes the $72 one-way fee. It is a pay-later reservation with cancellation allowed before pickup and no prepaid cancellation charge.
And the Birmingham return desk? I do not want a key drop creating a problem with a one-way rental.

The Avis counter at BHM is scheduled to remain staffed until 11:30 p.m. Wednesday. Your planned 3:30 p.m. return is during counter hours, and Avis confirmed that an agent can close the one-way contract at the desk. The rate permits return through 4:00 p.m. without a late charge.
Run the driving schedule once more, including the time-zone change Tuesday and the airport margin Wednesday.

Tuesday: arrive ATL at 10:15 a.m. Eastern, collect the car, and target departure by 11:10. That supports arrival at the Atlanta-area site around noon and inspection from noon to 2:00. Afterward, allow about 2 hours 25 minutes of driving; because Birmingham is one hour behind Atlanta, expected hotel arrival is about 3:25 p.m. Central without a stop or 3:45 with a short stop.

Wednesday: leave Home2 at 8:25 a.m., reach the restaurant before 9:00, and inspect until 1:30. Lunch can follow, but leave by 2:50 if it runs long. That leaves time to refuel and return the car at 3:30, about 2 hours 5 minutes before the 5:35 departure.
Good. Book the flights, Home2, and Avis at those totals. No optional rental coverage.

Before I submit: airfare is $624, Home2 is $211.44 with parking, and Avis is $274.62 including the $72 one-way fee. With $31 estimated fuel, total trip exposure is $1,141.06 before meals. Optional rental coverage is excluded. Shall I complete the purchase?

All three components are confirmed for September 16-17.

Flights: ORD-ATL 7:10-10:15 a.m. Tuesday and BHM-ORD 5:35-7:40 p.m. Wednesday, $624, confirmation Q7L3VD. The ticket is nonrefundable, with cancellation value retained as airline credit under the fare rules.

Hotel: Home2 Suites Birmingham Downtown, one king studio for Tuesday night, $196.44 including taxes plus $15 parking, confirmation H2-846317. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. Central on September 15; the penalty afterward is one night.

Rental: Avis midsize, ATL pickup Tuesday and BHM return Wednesday, $274.62, confirmation AV-592804. The total includes the $72 one-way fee; optional coverage was declined. The BHM counter is staffed until 11:30 p.m., and the planned 3:30 p.m. return is within both counter hours and the rate’s 4:00 p.m. return limit.

Final expected total is $1,141.06 including parking and estimated fuel, before meals. Tuesday’s intercity plan and Wednesday’s 8:25 departure, 2:50 lunch cutoff, refueling stop, and 3:30 car return remain workable.
